evidence.claim: Edenton faces Albemarle Sound; south of Windsor, the Sans Souci cable ferry carries two cars at a time across the Cashie River.
evidence.quote: The town of Edenton is located on the Albemarle Sound in North Carolina

evidence.claim: Water crossings have changed here: trains once traveled by ferry between Mackeys and Edenton.
evidence.quote: Prior to the Albemarle Sound Trestle being built, trains used to cross to Edenton via a ferry.

evidence.claim: In 1910, the Norfolk Southern Railroad built a wooden railway trestle between them.
evidence.quote: In 1910 the Norfolk Southern Railroad built a wooden trestle bridging the 5.05 mi from Mackeys to Edenton

evidence.claim: Maintenance costs ended its use in the late 1980s, and it was dismantled.
evidence.quote: In the late 1980s Norfolk Southern discontinued use of the Albemarle Sound Trestle due to maintenance costs and subsequently dismantled it.

evidence.claim: The Sans Souci crossing has operated in some form since at least the 1800s; the state transportation department took over in the 1930s.
evidence.quote: The Sans Souci Ferry has operated in some form or fashion since at least the 1800s. It was not until the 1930s that the state Department of Transportation took over operations of the ferry

evidence.claim: Windsor is the Bertie County seat, established at Gray’s Landing.
evidence.quote: Windsor is a town established by an act of the Colonial Assembly in 1768, on the site known as Gray’s Landing and is the county seat of Bertie County

evidence.claim: Mackeys lies on Albemarle Sound’s south side, while Pea Ridge is near the Albemarle Sound Bridge.
evidence.quote: Mackeys Ferry is located in North Carolina's Inner Banks region and is located at the mouth of the Mackeys Creek on the south side of the Albemarle Sound.

evidence.claim: Edenton occupies the north end of Edenton Bay.
evidence.quote: Edenton is located in southern Chowan County sits at the north end of Edenton Bay

evidence.quote: The ferry carries a maximum of two cars

evidence.claim: Windsor took shape at a place already known as Gray’s Landing, becoming a town by an act of the Colonial Assembly in 1768.
evidence.quote: Windsor is a town established by an act of the Colonial Assembly in 1768, on the site known as Gray’s Landing

evidence.claim: It is the seat of Bertie County.
evidence.quote: is the county seat of Bertie County

evidence.claim: The courthouse was built in 1889, a brick Neoclassical building with a polygonal cupola above its gable roof.
evidence.quote: It was built in 1889, and is a 2 1/2-story, brick Neoclassical-style building with a gable roof topped by a polygonal cupola.

evidence.claim: Its portico was enlarged and wings added in 1941, followed by a rear addition in 1974.
evidence.quote: In 1941, the portico was enlarged and wings added to the main block.  A rear addition was built in 1974.

evidence.claim: The surrounding historic district includes residential, commercial and institutional buildings dating primarily from after the turn of the 20th century.
evidence.quote: It includes residential, commercial, and institutional buildings that primarily date after the turn of the 20th century.

evidence.claim: The courthouse’s polygonal cupola rises above a gable roof.
evidence.quote: with a gable roof topped by a polygonal cupola.

evidence.claim: Fifty-one women in Edenton, led by Penelope Barker, signed a petition in 1774 to boycott English tea and other products.
evidence.quote: Fifty-one women in Edenton, led by Penelope Barker, signed a protest petition agreeing to boycott English tea and other products

evidence.claim: The action became known decades later as the Edenton Tea Party.
evidence.quote: in what became known, decades later, as the Edenton Tea Party.

evidence.claim: London newspapers responded with etchings depicting the women as uncontrollable.
evidence.quote: newspapers published etchings depicting the women as uncontrollable.

evidence.claim: The Barker House, Penelope Barker’s home, interprets colonial history as a house museum.
evidence.quote: The Barker House, home of Penelope Barker, the organizer of the first political action by women in the colonies, is operated as a house museum and to interpret colonial history.

evidence.claim: Another waterfront building, the Cupola House, was built by Francis Corbin in 1758 and stands there today.
evidence.quote: The Cupola House, a registered National Historic Landmark, was built by Francis Corbin in 1758 on the waterfront at Edenton where it stands today.

evidence.claim: The Sans Souci ferry follows a steel cable stretched across the Cashie River.
evidence.quote: The ferry is driven, or one could say guided, by a steel cable that stretches across the river.

evidence.claim: Normally submerged, the cable rises from the water as the boat moves, assisted by rollers on its side.
evidence.quote: As the ferry crosses the river, the force of the boat, with the help of rollers on the side of the boat, pulls the normally submerged cable out of the water.

evidence.claim: The cable stays attached to the ferry and holds it on course in normal currents.
evidence.quote: The cable is permanently secured to the ferry and prevents the boat from straying off course in normal river currents.

evidence.claim: Drivers on the opposite bank summon it with their vehicle horn.
evidence.quote: Persons wanting to ride the ferry that happen to be on the opposite side of the river than the ferry must blow their vehicle horn to summon the ferry.

evidence.claim: The crossing takes roughly five minutes and saves a drive of about 20 miles.
evidence.quote: The trip by ferry across the river takes roughly 5 minutes and saves a drive of about 20 miles.

evidence.claim: The ferry’s rollers lift its normally submerged guide cable as the boat crosses.
evidence.quote: As the ferry crosses the river, the force of the boat, with the help of rollers on the side of the boat, pulls the normally submerged cable out of the water.

evidence.claim: The ferry carries no more than two cars and does not operate in high water or storms.
evidence.quote: The ferry carries a maximum of two cars and does not operate in high water conditions or storms

evidence.claim: It entered the National Register in 1982, encompassing 78 contributing buildings.
evidence.quote: It encompasses 78 contributing buildings

evidence.claim: It entered the National Register in 1982
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982.

evidence.claim: The boycott supported the organizers of the Boston Tea Party.
evidence.quote: a protest organized by several Edenton women in 1774 in solidarity with the organizers of the Boston Tea Party.

evidence.claim: The Cupola House became a National Historic Landmark in 1970.
evidence.quote: Edenton is home to numerous early houses and public buildings, including the Cupola House. It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1970

evidence.claim: The operator controls a diesel engine, but the boat has neither brakes nor an onboard steering device.
evidence.quote: The ferry is powered by a John Deere diesel engine. The operator must know when to let off the throttle, since the ferry has no brakes or on-board steering device.

evidence.claim: Regional DOT offices administer these inland cable ferries separately from the coastal ferry system.
evidence.quote: The NC cable ferries are considered inland ferries. They are operated by regional DOT divisional offices instead of the NC DOT Ferry Division.
